what: Four concept pictures of the step-by-step guide (Project_Guide.pdf): every number shown in a picture, the two rules that picked the real examples and what they chose, and the lettering check of each picture.

guide_nse.title: What the score NSE means
guide_nse.footnote: The NSE compares the errors of a forecast with the errors of 'always the average' (errors are squared, so large ones count most): no error gives 1, errors as large as those of the average give 0. French Broad, North Carolina, 2 January 2009 to 22 January 2009. These are the scores of this stretch, not of the report: the scores of the report cover all test years.

guide_lstm_cell.title: The memory of an LSTM, day by day
guide_lstm_cell.footnote: Each tap is a gate: a number between 0 (shut) and 1 (open) that the network learns to set from the day's inputs. What is passed on is a copy: the memory itself goes on to tomorrow. The network of the project has 64 such cells, and the forecast is made from what all of them pass on.

guide_gradient.footnote: An illustration with a made-up curve, not data of the project: six steps in each panel from the same start (hollow dot: the start; dark dot: after six steps). A real network has thousands of weights and does this for all of them at once.

example_of_the_pipeline.rule: of the test-year onsets warned 1 day ahead (river at or below its high-flow level when the forecast was made, forecast for the next day above it, and the river did rise above it), the one with the most rain on the day the forecast was made

stretch_of_the_score_picture.rule: river: the example river of the project; stretch: 5 days before to 15 days after an onset of the test years, no second onset inside; of these the one whose NSE 1 day ahead is closest to the median NSE of the 12 basins over all test years (results/lstm_all.json: sets.wq.test.summary.l1.nse_median)

notes: guide_pipeline.png shows ONE real forecast of the LSTM with the river gauge (prediction set lstm_wq), picked by the rule under example_of_the_pipeline.rule: it shows the path from the inputs to a warning, not how often a warning comes in time (114 of the 611 onsets of the test years were warned 1 day ahead).

guide_nse.png: the three scores are those of the days drawn, computed here with flood.nse; they are not scores of the report. Over all test years this river scores 0.50 and the median of the 12 basins is 0.59. 'Always the average' is the average of the days drawn, so its score is exactly 0.

The stretch of guide_nse.png was picked by the rule under stretch_of_the_score_picture.rule from 35 stretches around an onset; their scores run from -0.23 to 0.58 (median 0.12), so a forecast around an onset usually scores lower than the one drawn.
guide_lstm_cell.png is a drawing of the logic of one memory cell (torch.nn.LSTM as flood.LSTMNet uses it), not of data; the network of the project has 64 such cells.
guide_gradient.png is an illustration with a made-up curve and made-up learning rates: no number in it is a result of the project.
